summary: A revised specification of the Mail Transfer Protocol, an early protocol for delivering mail between hosts. It was itself superseded by the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. Replaced by RFC 788.

eli5.summary: Rules for how computers hand email to each other, like mail carriers swapping bags. A simpler set of rules soon replaced these.

subtitle: A protocol for transferring email between computers, with relay and multi-recipient support.

tldr.problem: Early computer mail systems needed a standard way to transfer messages between different computers and networks, handling cases where mail must be relayed through intermediate hosts.
tldr.mechanism: MTP uses a sender-MTP and receiver-MTP model with a MAIL command that specifies source routing (FROM path) and destination routing (TO path). Mail text is sent after the command and terminated with a period. Multi-recipient mail can be handled in two schemes: recipients-first or text-first.
tldr.outcome: Email could be transferred reliably across early Internet networks with support for relaying. RFC 788 later superseded it with a simpler version.

facts.label: Transport-independent
facts.value: Works over TCP, NCP, X.25, others

today: RFC 780 is a historical mail protocol. RFC 788 soon replaced it. The Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) later became the standard for email delivery.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The Mail Transfer Protocol (MTP) reliably transfers mail between computers. Unlike FTP which was designed for file transfer by users, MTP is designed for mail systems to exchange messages. It is independent of the underlying transport service and can work over TCP, NCP, or other reliable ordered data stream channels. A key feature is MTP's ability to relay mail through intermediate hosts when source and destination computers are not on the same network.
sections.eli5: MTP is the post office protocol: it lets mail computer talk to mail computer, and if the destination isn't on your network, it passes the letter along.

sections.title: The MTP Model
sections.content: MTP uses a sender-MTP and receiver-MTP model. The sender-MTP initiates a full-duplex transmission channel and sends commands. The receiver-MTP responds with replies. The core command is MAIL with a FROM path (the sender's mailbox and return route) and a TO path (destination mailbox and routing information for relaying). The sender then transmits the mail text, which terminates with a line containing only a period. The receiver responds with a numeric code indicating success or failure.
sections.eli5: One mail computer talks to another: 'I have mail from Alice for Bob', and if the other computer says yes, the mail is sent. If the destination is far away, the path tells it where to forward the mail.

sections.title: Multi-Recipient and Replies
sections.content: MTP supports sending one message to multiple recipients efficiently through two negotiable schemes. In recipients-first mode, each recipient is specified and acknowledged before the text is sent. In text-first mode, the text is sent first, then recipients are specified individually. Replies are three-digit numeric codes (like 250 for success or 354 to indicate 'start mail input') followed by text. The numeric code allows automation; the text is for human users.
sections.eli5: For multiple recipients, MTP can either ask 'who do you want?' then send the message, or send the message then ask 'who gets it?'. Either way, each destination either accepts or rejects.

references.text: Sluizer, S., and J. Postel, "Mail Transfer Protocol," RFC 772, August 1980.
